subject.title: fix(backup): write backup archive with owner-only 0o600 permissions

question: Should new `openclaw backup create` archives default to owner-only `0o600`, accepting that group/shared-reader backup collectors may need to run as the owner or chmod/copy after creation?
rationale: The patch fixes local credential exposure in a sensitive backup artifact, but it deliberately changes the shipped CLI artifact's file-permission semantics for newly created backups.

options.title: Accept owner-only default
options.body: Proceed with this PR after exact-head checks because backup archives contain credentials and should default to owner-only access.

options.title: Add transition guidance
options.body: Ask for PR-body or release-note wording before merge if maintainers want documented guidance for shared backup collection jobs.

options.title: Pause for another contract
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers want an explicit export/share mode instead of tightening the default artifact permissions unconditionally.

recommendation.title: Accept owner-only default
recommendation.body: Proceed with this PR after exact-head checks because backup archives contain credentials and should default to owner-only access.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and materially hardened the original backup CLI feature branch, so they are the best history-based owner for accepting the permission-default tradeoff.
